items.s: Bartholomew caught one of three targets for five yards in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. With T.J. Hockenson back in the lineup after being inactive Week 10, Bartholomew played just 18 of 67 offensive snaps as the Vikings' third tight end, also behind Ben Yurosek. Bartholomew has 11 catches for 95 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets across 10 games this season.

items.h: Set for lesser role in Week 11
items.s: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports. Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

items.h: Gavin Bartholomew catches touchdown in Week 10
items.s: Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and one touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10. Bartholomew has struggled to make an impact in the Minnesota offense to this point, recording four or more targets for the second time in nine games. The tight end can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 11 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

items.h: Gavin Bartholomew a Must-Add in Revamped Offense?
items.s: Minnesota Vikings tight end Gavin Bartholomew was not a household name until this past week, when his snap share soared to 77% and he ended up catching three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown. Bartholomew stepped up as the Vikings' No. 1 tight end with T.J. Hockenson (wrist, check) sidelined, and he wasted no time making an impact. In addition to taking on a bigger role with Hockenson out, the second-year tight end benefitted from a quarterback upgrade. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) injured and Carson Wentz struggling, the Vikings decided to trade for Kirk Cousins, and the veteran immediately developed a rapport with Bartholomew. Hockenson could end up being healthy for Week 11…

Bartholomew caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. With T.J. Hockenson (wrist) inactive, Bartholomew played 53 of 69 offensive snaps against Green Bay and caught the second of Kirk Cousins' two touchdowns, scoring from 20 yards out in the fourth quarter to give Minnesota a comfortable 27-10 lead. While Ben Yurosek got the start, Bartholomew played 13 more snaps and out-targeted Yurosek four to one. Cousins has an affinity for throwing to his tight ends, so Bartholomew will be on the fantasy radar if Hockenson needs to miss more time.

items.h: Gavin Bartholomew catches five passes in Week 5 win
items.s: Gavin Bartholomew caught five of his six targets for 33 yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. Bartholomew took advantage of the concussion suffered by T.J. Hockenson early in the contest, finishing second in targets and receiving yards in the win. The tight end's value remains tied to the health of No. 1 T.J. Hockenson as the Vikings enter a Week 6 bye.

Bartholomew saw one target in Saturday's preseason opener against the Giants. The tight end logged 31 percent of the Vikings' offensive snaps in the contest. Bartholomew was in for 18 offensive plays but was unable to snag a reception. The 23-year-old will likely remain behind Ben Yurosek on the depth chart as the two head into their sophomore season with the Vikings.

Bartholomew (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers. Bartholomew spent the 2025 season on the reserve/PUP list and will officially not be available for Week 18. The sixth-round pick out of Pittsburgh will have to look towards the 2026 season for his first opportunity to play in an NFL game.

Bartholomew (back) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Giants. Bartholomew was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game after logging back-to-back full practice sessions, but he nonetheless won't come off the reserve/PUP list yet. The rookie sixth-round pick's next opportunity to retake the field will come in Week 17 versus the Lions on Thursday night.

Bartholomew (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Giants. Bartholomew ended Week 16 prep with back-to-back full practices to earn the questionable tag. He opened the season on the physically unable to perform list due to a back injury he sustained in late August, so he'd have to be activated from the Vikings' PUP list Saturday in order to be available for Sunday's contest. If that happens, the rookie sixth-rounder would be slated to make his NFL regular-season debut in New York.

Bartholomew (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. Bartholomew has yet to make his NFL debut. The sixth-round pick out of Pittsburgh has remained on the PUP list all year due to a back injury he suffered in late August. With a limited practice Wednesday that upgraded to a full session Thursday, it seems the rookie tight end could be a depth addition to the Vikings' offense as early as Sunday's game against the Giants.

Bartholomew (back) was designated to return from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday. The rookie tight end from Pittsburgh was placed on the PUP list in late August due to a back issue, but it now appears he's nearing a return. Bartholomew has yet to make his NFL debut after posting 322 receiving yards and four touchdowns on 38 receptions during his final collegiate season. Once fully healthy, he'll likely play a depth role in the Vikings' tight-end corps.

Bartholomew (back) was placed on the reserve/PUP list Tuesday. The rookie sixth-round pick out of Pittsburgh missed the entire training camp and will now sit out at least four games. Bartholomew put together a solid collegiate career but never surpassed 326 yards or four touchdowns in a season. Once he returns, he'll look to usurp undrafted rookie Benjamin Yurosek for the No. 3 tight end job.

Coach Kevin O'Connell said Tuesday that Bartholomew is dealing with a lower back injury, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. Bartholomew was placed on the active/PUP list Monday. The sixth-round rookie also missed a decent chunk of the offseason program rehabbing an injury.

items.h: Gavin Bartholomew placed on PUP list
items.s: The Vikings placed Gavin Bartholomew on the PUP list ahead of training camp. Bartholomew was the No. 202 overall selection back in April. He can be activated at any point during camp.

items.h: Bartholomew (undisclosed) was placed on the active/PUP list by the Vikings on Monday.
items.s: Once the tight end is able to resume practicing, he can return at any point during training camp and the preseason. Bartholomew was rehabbing an undisclosed injury during the Vikings' offseason program in June. Minnesota selected the Pittsburgh product in the sixth round of April's draft, though he's clearly behind T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver on the depth chart.

items.h: Bartholomew was off to the side rehabbing an undisclosed injury during the recent offseason program, Will Ragatz of Sports Illustrated reports.
items.s: It's likely a minor injury, but it's something to watch at the start of training camp. Bartholomew is a 2025 sixth-round draft pick, so his roster spot isn't guaranteed and a slow start to training camp due to injury could hurt his chances.

items.h: The Vikings selected Bartholomew in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, 202nd overall.
items.s: Bartholomew (6-foot-5, 246 pounds) likely won't prove to be any more than a backup in the NFL, but he had a respectable collegiate career at Pittsburgh, where he was a four-year starter. The problem is that Bartholomew just doesn't stand out in any way -- his production from his true freshman season (28 receptions for 326 yards and four touchdowns) was arguably a career year, and it's not usually a great sign if a player's best season is their true freshman one. With that said, Bartholomew's 4.7-second 40-yard dash is completely respectable and there's no obvious reason why he can't stick…
